issues.item: Triggers: Being Followed: Feeling followed or tracked
issues.explanation: 'Being followed or tracked' is difficult to reconcile with the stated trauma type of trauma to a loved one and with the rest of the profile, which centers on grief, guilt, and generalized somatic alarm rather than a pursuit/persecution context. It stands apart from the other trigger items and does not connect plausibly to the memory content provided.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Fear Going Crazy: My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy
issues.explanation: 'My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy' is not well aligned with the rest of the formulation and item set. The profile otherwise emphasizes guilt, grief, misery, fragmented/numb recall, and bodily false alarms after a loved-one trauma. A 'going crazy' appraisal is possible, but here it appears weakly supported by the trigger and memory content and feels clinically out of step relative to the otherwise bereavement/guilt-focused presentation.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Life Not Worth Living: I am not sure my life is worth living anymore
issues.explanation: For trauma to a loved one, severe guilt, misery, and a sense that life has been destroyed can be coherent. However, the specific appraisal 'I am not sure my life is worth living anymore' is notably more global and suicidal in tone than the rest of the selected profile, and it is not supported by corresponding threat, memory, trigger, or strategy content. With the provided five components, this item stands out as insufficiently anchored to the rest of the formulation-relevant material, making the node less internally coherent.

vignette: Kai had always been a happy-go-lucky person, but that all changed when his younger brother died in a tragic accident. It was a night that Kai would never forget, yet he struggled to piece together the events leading up to the tragedy. Whenever he tried to recall the details, he felt intense guilt wash over him, as if he could have done something to prevent it. The memories were fragmented and disjointed, making it impossible for him to form a coherent narrative. As Kai navigated his daily life as a pharmacist, he found himself constantly on edge. His body would react before his mind even had time to process the situation, leaving him feeling like he was walking on eggshells. He would often catch himself tensing up at the slightest sound or smell, especially the pungent aroma of alcohol, which instantly transported him back to that fateful night. The smell would trigger a cascade of memories, each one more disturbing than the last. Kai's perception of the world had changed dramatically since his brother's death. He now saw people misbehaving as a constant threat, and funerals or graves seemed to be everywhere he looked. Even the simplest tasks felt like a struggle, as if he was just going through the motions. His friends and family noticed the change in him too; they would comment on how miserable he always seemed, how nothing seemed to bring him joy anymore. As Kai reflected on his life, he couldn't help but feel that it had been destroyed by the trauma. He felt lost and without direction, as if everything he had once found meaningful was now just a distant memory. This sense of hopelessness only served to heighten his threat monitoring, making him even more vigilant for potential dangers lurking around every corner. Kai's negative appraisals about himself and the world had become self-reinforcing, fueling his hypervigilance and making it increasingly difficult for him to shake off the feeling of being constantly on edge. His body was always tense, ready to react to the next perceived threat, which in turn reinforced his negative thoughts about the world. The vicious cycle was exhausting, both mentally and physically. Kai felt like he was trapped in a never-ending nightmare, unable to wake up or escape the memories that haunted him. It was this overwhelming sense of despair that finally drove him to seek help, hoping to break free from the grip of his trauma and find some semblance of peace once again. As he sat in the therapist's office, Kai couldn't help but wonder if he would ever be able to reclaim his lost happiness or find meaning in a world that seemed so cruel and unforgiving. The journey ahead would be long and arduous, but for the first time in months, Kai felt a glimmer of hope - a sense that maybe, just maybe, he could learn to live with his memories and find a way to heal.
